newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank will guard CZK against external forces.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank will guard CZK against external forces.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Wednesday it was prepared to defend the crown from being weakened too much by external forces, the Czech news agency CTK reported on Wednesday.

"Causes of the development (of the crown) stand outside the Czech economy...This does not have a connection with our economy and the central bank would if needed protect the currency from such external influences," CTK quoted CNB spokesman Martin Svehla as saying.

The crown weakened about one percentage point against its dollar/mark basket midpoint on Wednesday. It was trading at around 3.8 percent on the depreciation of basket parity in late afternoon trading.
Last week, CNB officials said they were prepared to raise interest rates if needed to defend the crown from weakening too much, though they did not say at what point this would occur.
At midday, the CNB fixed the crown at 3.58 percent on the depreciation side of basket parity, after fixing it at -2.61 percent on Tuesday.
The crown has been very volatile in recent weeks after a fresh wave of poor economic data emphasised market concerns that the Czech economy was headed for a sharp downturn.

On Monday, the statistical bureau (CSU) said that industrial output, as it had done in the previous two months, contracted, shrinking 2.5 percent, year-on-year in March. Output for the first quarter was down 4.2 percent.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus has said that he expects first quarter GDP growth -- due to be released on June 19 -- would probably be "about zero percent".
Czech GDP grew 4.4 percent, year-on-year, in 1996, and was originally forecast to grow 5.4 percent this year but Klaus, a monetarist economist, has said growth of 2.7 percent would be a "success".
